title: Sparse snapshot detection and atomic chunk resume for scheduled usage CSV exports
creator: Jenna Park
description:
Problem: Large scheduled CSV exports for customers with sparse activity create huge files dominated by empty/zero rows, leading to wasted bandwidth, high S3 storage costs, and long upload times that increase the probability of multipart upload failures. When uploads fail partway through, current retry logic replays overlapping chunks and sometimes duplicates rows or stalls until manual intervention.

Goal: Implement a sparse-snapshot detector that compacts export payloads by eliding contiguous zero-activity ranges and encode compact segments in the manifest, and add an atomic chunk-resume mechanism for multipart uploads so a failed export can resume from the last committed chunk without duplication. Keep webhook delivery semantics unchanged (exactly-once visible exports) and ensure backfills and downstream consumers (analytics pipeline, billing) are unaffected.

Scope: server-side export generator, manifest schema v2, uploader (multipart/Resumable S3 multipart + signed-URL orchestration), webhook delivery ack semantics, console progress tracking, and test harness for large synthetic tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Export manifest v2 supports 'segments' with start/end raw time windows and compacted-row-count metadata
Exports with >60% sparse rows reduce S3 size by >=50% in benchmark datasets
Failed multipart uploads can be resumed atomically at chunk boundaries without duplicate rows and the export status remains 'failed' until manifest commit completes
Webhook delivery uses the same delivery contract: webhook receives a manifest URL and size estimates; no semantic change to downstream consumers
Console shows per-export chunk progress and a resumable checkbox; operators can force resume or restart from last committed chunk
E2E tests covering resume, duplicate suppression, and manifest consumers (billing/analytics) are added and green
design_notes: We will keep the blob format CSV-compatible by storing compacted segments as normal CSV rows but record sparse ranges in the manifest so consumers that need a time-series can reconstruct implicit zero rows if desired. Manifest v2 will include a checksum per segment (CRC32c) and an overall manifest checksum for idempotency. The uploader will keep an ordered list of chunk checksums and an 'upload cursor' stored in Redis to coordinate resumable multipart uploads across coordinator restarts. Use existing tenant-partitioned upload prefixes (s3://redwood-exports/{tenant}/v2/{export_id}/chunks/). Avoid changing public webhook contract: webhook still receives a signed manifest URL; manifest v2 is backwards compatible (older consumers ignore 'segments' field).
implementation_plan: Add a sparse-snapshot compaction step to export generator: detect contiguous zero rows (config threshold 10% run length as default) and emit segment descriptors
Bump manifest schema to v2 and include per-segment metadata (start_ts,end_ts,row_count,compacted:true,crc32c)
Implement chunk-resume state machine in export-orchestrator: save cursor after each committed part in Redis and S3 manifest-temp path
Update multipart uploader to verify part checksums before commit and to allow commit-at-part-index API
Preserve webhook contract; update console to display 'resumable' and 'compacted' flags
Add feature flag 'exports.compaction' gated by org-level config for 2-week rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests: compaction thresholds, manifest v2 schema validation, checksum validation
Integration: synthetic tenant with 10M rows and 95% zero rows; compare raw vs compacted size and validate reconstruction logic
Failure injection: interrupt uploads at each multipart boundary and assert resume yields identical canonical CSV after reconstruction
Downstream regression tests: billing pipeline input parity, analytics job identity-preservation
Performance: measure export generator CPU/memory and upload latency with compaction enabled vs disabled
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag. Week 0: deploy compaction code path to canary namespace for non-critical orgs. Week 1: enable for 10% of tenants with small-activity heuristics; monitor S3 storage delta and export latencies. Week 2: expand to 50% and then full enable for tenants opted in. If we detect >2% rate of resume anomalies or >5% increase in billing pipeline lag, rollback the flag.
comments: 2025-09-14 - Jenna Park: Triage: reported repeated multipart upload cost and duplication during retries for very large scheduled exports. Attached perf traces and an initial hypothesis (compaction + resumable commits).

2025-09-17 - Luis Ortega: Design review: prefer manifest-level compact segments rather than changing CSV layout. Will add per-segment CRC and Redis-based upload cursor. Blocking question on downstream consumers -- tagging @Priya for billing validation.

2025-09-19 - Priya Nair (billing): Confirmed billing accepts manifest v2 as long as export consumer can expand compacted segments; agreed to add reconstruction helper in billing repo. No billing schema changes required.

2025-09-23 - Luis Ortega: Implemented compaction prototype and synthetic benchmark. Result: 68% S3 size reduction for sparse tenant fixture, CPU overhead ~8% on generator. Pushed prototype PR 8921 for initial review.
2025-09-25 - Security Review: Ran quick review; no PII changes. Decided not to require formal security review for v1 compaction (security_review_required=false).

2025-09-29 - QA (Anita Desai): Started failure-injection tests. Found an edge case: when Redis cursor expires during long commit, resume logic attempted to start from 0. Added TTL refresh in orchestrator and defensive checks.
2025-10-01 - Luis Ortega: Addressed TTL issue and added idempotent commit checks. Ready for integration tests on staging. Plan to enable feature flag for 10% canary on 2025-10-05.
2025-10-02 - Jenna Park: Updated acceptance criteria to require chunk checksums and console visibility. Added monitoring dashboards to detect regressions post-rollout.
